## 2026-11-02: ML24088A065 Nuclear Island systems (PSAR design basis)

Systems and components from the Chapter 7 contents and figure list and Section 1.1.4, using the PSAR's names. Purpose questions use distractors that are purposes of other systems in this list (systems with overlapping purposes are never used as each other's distractors). Function questions are included only where the PSAR states the link.

- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Core System (RCC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Sustain a nuclear chain reaction for fission heat generation
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.1, p. 1.1-3 (PDF page 33)
  - Quote: "The RCC is designed to sustain a nuclear chain reaction for fission heat generation within the thermal-mechanical constraints of the components (e.g., fuel, cladding, structures)."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.1) describes this purpose for Reactor Core System (RCC). The other options are purposes of Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC), Reactor Enclosure System (RES), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Enclosure System (RES) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Support the reactor core and contain the primary sodium coolant
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.2, p. 1.1-3 (PDF page 33)
  - Quote: "The RES supports the reactor core and contains the primary sodium coolant."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.2) describes this purpose for Reactor Enclosure System (RES). The other options are purposes of Main Control Room (MCR), Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST), and Nuclear Island Auxiliary Electrical Systems.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Guard Vessel (GV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Provide a defense-in-depth coolant and functional containment boundary if the reactor vessel leaks
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1.3, p. 7.1-16 (PDF page 1213)
  - Quote: "The RV is surrounded by a GV, which provides a defense-in-depth coolant and functional containment boundary in the unlikely occurrence of RV leakage."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.1.2.1.3) describes this purpose for Guard Vessel (GV). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island E-Modules, Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Provide passive decay heat removal to the environment by natural convection of air
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.3, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The RAC primary objective is to provide passive decay heat removal to the environment through natural convection of air."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.3) describes this purpose for Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC). The other options are purposes of NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD), Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST), and NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Transport heat from the reactor core to the Intermediate Heat Transport System
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.4, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The principal function of the PHT is to transport heat from the reactor core to the IHT for use in power generation."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.4) describes this purpose for Primary Heat Transport System (PHT). The other options are purposes of Reactor Protection System (RPS), Reactor Core System (RCC), and Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Provide the head to drive primary sodium flow
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.3.2.1, p. 7.1-57 (PDF page 1254)
  - Quote: "During normal operations, plant startup and shutdown, and during certain LBEs, the PSPs provide the necessary head to drive primary sodium flow."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.1.3.2.1) describes this purpose for Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs). The other options are purposes of Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP), Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC), and NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Heat Exchangers (IHXs) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Transfer heat from the primary sodium to the intermediate sodium
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.3.3.1, p. 7.1-59 (PDF page 1256)
  - Quote: "There are two IHXs in the PHT that transfer heat from the primary sodium of the PHT to the intermediate sodium of IHT"
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.1.3.3.1) describes this purpose for Intermediate Heat Exchangers (IHXs). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting, Sodium Processing System (SPS), and Nuclear Island E-Modules.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Transport heat away from the PHT to the salt system or to the air coolers
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.5, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The IHT primary function is to transport heat away from the PHT. The IHT delivers the heat removed from the PHT to the NSS for energy storage or electrical power generation, or to the IAC to be rejected as waste heat to the atmosphere."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.5) describes this purpose for Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT). The other options are purposes of Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST), Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Transfer heat from the intermediate sodium loops to the atmosphere
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.6, p. 1.1-5 (PDF page 35)
  - Quote: "The IAC is the preferred heat removal system for the reactor during upset events. The IAC transfers heat from the IHT to the atmosphere."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.6) describes this purpose for Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC). The other options are purposes of Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST), Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB), and In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Salt System (NSS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Remove heat from the IHT sodium-salt heat exchangers into the molten salt loop
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.2.1, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "Heat is removed from the IHT SHXs in the RAB by the NSS to ESS to TSS molten salt loop during reactor operation."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.2.1) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Salt System (NSS). The other options are purposes of Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC), Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Control, monitor and supply inert argon gas to systems and components in the RXB, RAB and FHB
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.7, p. 1.1-5 (PDF page 35)
  - Quote: "The SCG controls, monitors, and supplies inert argon gas to various systems and components throughout the Reactor Building (RXB), Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB), and Fuel Handling Building (FHB)."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.7) describes this purpose for Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG). The other options are purposes of Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT), Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC), and Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Processing System (SPS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Monitor and remove contaminants such as cesium, oxygen and hydrogen from the liquid sodium
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.8, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The Sodium Processing System (SPS) monitors and removes contaminants including cesium and compounds including oxygen and hydrogen from the liquid sodium inventory."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.8) describes this purpose for Sodium Processing System (SPS). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB), Main Control Room (MCR), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Control Rod Drive System (CRD) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Provide core reactivity control for power control, power shaping and reactor shutdown
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.9, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The purpose of the CRD is to provide core reactivity control for the purpose of core power control, power shaping, and reactor shutdown."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.9) describes this purpose for Control Rod Drive System (CRD). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Distributed Control System (DCS), Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC), and Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Protection System (RPS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Automatically generate output signals to initiate reactor scram and engineered safety feature functions
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.11, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The primary function of the RPS is to, with precision and reliability, accept input signals from plant instrumentation, apply necessary logic, and automatically generate output signals to initiate safety functions including reactor scram and engineered safety feature functions when required by plant conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.11) describes this purpose for Reactor Protection System (RPS). The other options are purposes of Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC), Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC), and Radiation Monitoring System (RMS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Sense neutron flux leakage from the core
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.12, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS) provides instrumentation to sense neutron flux leakage from the core during fuel movement, reactor startup, power operations, shutdown, and accident conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.12) describes this purpose for Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS). The other options are purposes of NI Heat Tracing System (NHT), NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP), and Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Radiation Monitoring System (RMS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Provide radiation activity indications for systems, buildings and release pathways to protect personnel and the environment
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The Radiation Monitoring System (RMS) provides radiation activity indications for systems, buildings, and release pathways throughout the plant at strategic interface points for use in the protection of plant personnel and the surrounding environment during all operating conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.13) describes this purpose for Radiation Monitoring System (RMS). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island E-Modules, Seismic Monitoring System (SMS), and Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Measure parameters such as hot pool level and temperature and send them to the RPS and NIC
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.14, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS) provides measurements for parameters and sends these signals in an appropriate format to RPS, and NIC, for control, safety functions, post-accident monitoring, and informational purposes."
  - Quote: "Parameters include hot pool level, hot pool temperature, cold pool temperature, and PSP shaft speed."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.14) describes this purpose for Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH), Primary Heat Transport System (PHT), and Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Control System (NIC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Group the non-safety I&C subsystems (RMC, CTC, UMC, AMC, FHC, PMC) that control the Nuclear Island
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.15, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The NIC is a group of I&C subsystems that perform non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST) and NSRST functions."
  - Quote: "The subsystems that are part of the NIC include the Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC), the Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC), the Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC), the Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC), the Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC), and the Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC)."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.15) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Control System (NIC). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB), Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG), and Primary Heat Transport System (PHT).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Distributed Control System (DCS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Gather information from field sensors, interfaces and other I&C systems as the primary NIC subsystem
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.5, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The DCS is the primary subsystem of the NIC and provides a means for gathering information from various sources, such as field sensors, human-system Interfaces (HSIs), and data feeds from other I&C systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.5) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Distributed Control System (DCS). The other options are purposes of Radiation Monitoring System (RMS), Primary Heat Transport System (PHT), and Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Control and monitor the primary and secondary control rod assemblies
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.16, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC) is a subsystem of the NIC that is used to control and monitor primary control rod assemblies and secondary control rod assemblies for all reactor operation modes."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.16) describes this purpose for Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC). The other options are purposes of Sodium Processing System (SPS), Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT), and Intermediate Heat Exchangers (IHXs).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Monitor and control the flow control functions of the PHT, IHT, NSS, IAC and ESS
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.17, p. 1.1-9 (PDF page 39)
  - Quote: "The CTC monitors and controls the PHT, IHT, NSS, IAC, and EI Salt Heat Transport System (ESS) flow control functions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.17) describes this purpose for Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC). The other options are purposes of Radiation Monitoring System (RMS), Intermediate Heat Exchangers (IHXs), and Nuclear Island Salt System (NSS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Monitor and control the auxiliary electrical and ancillary systems
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.2.1, p. 7.6-7 (PDF page 1435)
  - Quote: "Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC) – The UMC monitors and controls the various auxiliary electrical and ancillary systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.6.2.1) describes this purpose for Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC). The other options are purposes of Reactor Enclosure System (RES), Primary Heat Transport System (PHT), and Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Monitor and control Nuclear Island auxiliary systems such as radwaste, cover gas and sodium processing
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.2.1, p. 7.6-6 (PDF page 1434)
  - Quote: "Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC) – The AMC monitors and controls Nuclear Island (NI) auxiliary systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.6.2.1) describes this purpose for Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP), Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC), and Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Serve as the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system for fuel handling
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.20, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "The Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC) functions as the Supervisory, Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) for the fuel handling processes."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.20) describes this purpose for Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC). The other options are purposes of Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB), Reactor Enclosure System (RES), and Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Let operators monitor plant data and manually control equipment through the HMI, with no automatic control
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.21, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "The PMC provides plant operators the capability to monitor plant data and control plant equipment through the HMI in all operating modes. The PMC does not have ability to perform automatic control."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.1.21) describes this purpose for Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC). The other options are purposes of Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC), Nuclear Island Salt System (NSS), and NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Manipulate core assembly positions during refueling and maintain the primary functional containment boundary when installed
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.1, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "Together, these components manipulate the positions of core assemblies during refueling operations and maintain the primary functional containment boundary during all reactor modes when the equipment is installed."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.1) describes this purpose for In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI). The other options are purposes of Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC), Fuel Handling Building (FHB), and Control Rod Drive System (CRD).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHE) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Facilitate the receipt, conditioning, storage, installation and removal of all core assemblies
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.2, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "The Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHE) includes equipment that facilitates the receipt, conditioning, storage, installation, and removal of all core assemblies."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.2) describes this purpose for Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHE). The other options are purposes of NI normal lighting system, Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC), and Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Handling Machine (EVHM) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Transfer core assemblies in sodium-filled pots between the reactor vessel and the Ex-Vessel Storage Tank
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.1, p. 7.3-16 (PDF page 1365)
  - Quote: "It is used to transfer core assemblies (non-fuel, irradiated fuel, and non-irradiated fuel), contained within a liquid sodium filled core assembly pot (CAP), between the reactor vessel located in the Reactor Building (RXB) and the EVST located in the Fuel Handling Building (FHB)."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.3.2.1.1) describes this purpose for Ex-Vessel Handling Machine (EVHM). The other options are purposes of Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB), Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA), and Nuclear Island Plant Communication System.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Transfer core assemblies between the new assembly preconditioning station, the Pool Immersion Cell and the EVST
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.2, p. 7.3-18 (PDF page 1367)
  - Quote: "It is used to transfer core assemblies (non-fuel, irradiated fuel, and non-irradiated fuel), between the NAPS, Pool Immersion Cell and the EVST located in the FHB."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.3.2.1.2) describes this purpose for Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Plant Communication System, Primary Heat Transport System (PHT), and Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Provide a controlled sodium environment for temporary storage of new and irradiated core assemblies
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.3, p. 7.3-19 (PDF page 1368)
  - Quote: "Its function is to provide a controlled environment for temporary storage for new components in route to the reactor, and irradiated core assemblies removed from the reactor."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.3.2.1.3) describes this purpose for Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP), Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB), and In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Store irradiated core assemblies in a water-cooled pool
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.3, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "The Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP) consists of the subsystems and equipment necessary to store irradiated core assemblies within the water-cooled pool."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.3) describes this purpose for Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP). The other options are purposes of Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC), Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV), and NI normal lighting system.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Main Control Room (MCR) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Let operators initiate or take manual control of each function needed to control the plant and maintain safety
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.4, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The MCR contains equipment that is part of the NIC that allows operators to initiate or take manual control of each function necessary to control the plant and maintain safety."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.4) describes this purpose for Main Control Room (MCR). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH), NI Grounding and Earthing and Lightning Protection (NGL), and NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Provide a location to monitor safe shutdown conditions if the MCR is no longer habitable
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.4.1.1, p. 7.8-27 (PDF page 1545)
  - Quote: "the NCB substructure includes a location for the RSC, as described in Section 7.6.7.2, that is used to monitor plant safe shutdown conditions in case the MCR is no longer habitable."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.8.4.1.1) describes this purpose for Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC). The other options are purposes of Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC), Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL), and Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Auxiliary Electrical Systems as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Distribute auxiliary electrical power to the Nuclear Island
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NI electrical power distribution is divided into several systems to distribute auxiliary electrical power to the NI of Kemmerer Unit 1."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.6) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Auxiliary Electrical Systems. The other options are purposes of Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST), Ex-Vessel Handling Machine (EVHM), and Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Supply medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and the PSP and ISP adjustable speed drives
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NMV supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.6) describes this purpose for NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV). The other options are purposes of Radiation Monitoring System (RMS), Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG), and In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Supply 480V switchgear, motor control centers, switchboards and panelboards for NI auxiliary loads
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NLV supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.6) describes this purpose for NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV). The other options are purposes of Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG), Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC), and Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Heat Tracing System (NHT) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Power heating cables on process lines and tanks to prevent freezing and crystallization of fluids such as sodium and molten salt
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NI electrical system also includes an NHT that distributes power to heating cables on process lines and tanks to maintain specific fluid temperature to prevent freezing and crystallization of process fluids, such as molten salts, sodium, and water."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.6) describes this purpose for NI Heat Tracing System (NHT). The other options are purposes of Reactor Protection System (RPS), Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs), and Sodium Processing System (SPS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Provide uninterruptible AC power to NI loads such as the RPS, XIS, RMS and CRD motor controllers
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.1, p. 7.7-1 (PDF page 1509)
  - Quote: "The NUP provides uninterruptible AC power to NI loads, including the following:"
  - Quote: "Reactor Protection System and Post-Accident Monitoring cabinets (see Section 7.6.3) ● Nuclear Instrumentation System (see Section 7.6.4) ● Radiation Monitoring System (see Section 7.6.6) ● Control rod drive motor controllers"
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.7.1.1) describes this purpose for NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP). The other options are purposes of Reactor Enclosure System (RES), Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST), and NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI DC Power Supply System (NDC) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Provide continuous, stable DC power through four independent 250 VDC divisions, one per RPS division
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.3.2, p. 7.7-5 (PDF page 1513)
  - Quote: "For system reliability and to ensure continuous and stable uninterrupted electrical power is provided to NI systems and components, the NDC comprises four independent 250 VDC divisions - one for each Reactor Protection System division"
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.7.1.3.2) describes this purpose for NI DC Power Supply System (NDC). The other options are purposes of Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC), Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL), and Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Process cover gas waste streams and hold them up so radioactive isotopes such as argon-41 decay
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.7, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The RWG is located in the FHB and is a once-through system that processes the gaseous waste streams from primary SCG and the SCG exhaust distribution cabinet. The system provides holdup for the decay of short-lived radioactive isotopes such as Argon-41."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.7) describes this purpose for Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG). The other options are purposes of Primary Heat Transport System (PHT), Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB), and Main Control Room (MCR).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Collect, segregate, process, sample and monitor non-sodium, non-salt liquid radioactive waste
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.8, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The RWL is designed to collect, segregate, process, sample, and monitor the non-sodium and non-salt liquid radioactive waste for reuse or evaporation."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.8) describes this purpose for Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL). The other options are purposes of Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC), NI DC Power Supply System (NDC), and Control Rod Drive System (CRD).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Solid Radwaste Processing System (RWS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Process wet and dry solid waste from plant systems
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.9, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The RWS is designed to process both wet and dry solid waste from plant systems and sources."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.9) describes this purpose for Solid Radwaste Processing System (RWS). The other options are purposes of NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV), Radiation Monitoring System (RMS), and Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Provide HVAC for personnel comfort, freeze protection and equipment operability
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.10, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The NHV is provided as required for personnel comfort, freeze protection, and equipment operability in areas identified as requiring temperature control on a per-building basis."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.10) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP), NI Fire Suppression System (NFS), and NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI normal lighting system as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Provide general indoor and outdoor lighting during operation, maintenance and testing
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.11, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The normal lighting system provides illumination for general indoor and outdoor lighting during plant operation, maintenance, and test conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.11) describes this purpose for NI normal lighting system. The other options are purposes of In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI), Reactor Core System (RCC), and Ex-Vessel Handling Machine (EVHM).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Provide illumination in NI plant areas during a station blackout
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.17, p. 1.1-17 (PDF page 47)
  - Quote: "NI emergency operating lighting provides illumination in NI plant areas during an station blackout (SBO)"
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.17) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting. The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island E-Modules, Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST), and NI Heat Tracing System (NHT).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Grounding and Earthing and Lightning Protection (NGL) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Protect personnel and equipment from transient over-voltages and provide a ground reference for instrument signals
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.11, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The NGL provides protection of plant personnel and equipment from the effect of transient over-voltages that can occur in electrical systems, voltage surges due to electrical faults or lightning strikes, and provides a proper ground reference for the instrumentation signals."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.11) describes this purpose for NI Grounding and Earthing and Lightning Protection (NGL). The other options are purposes of Reactor Core System (RCC), Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB), and NI Fire Suppression System (NFS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Plant Communication System as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Provide an independent means of onsite and offsite communication in all modes, including emergencies
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.12, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The NI communication system is designed to provide an independent means of effective onsite and offsite communication during all modes of plant operation, including during abnormal and emergency operating conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.12) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Plant Communication System. The other options are purposes of Guard Vessel (GV), Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs), and NI Fire Suppression System (NFS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Lift and move approved loads within NI buildings
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.13, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The NCH primary function is to lift and move approved loads within the NI buildings to support normal operations, maintenance, and other required activities."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.13) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH). The other options are purposes of NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV), NI DC Power Supply System (NDC), and Reactor Core System (RCC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Air and Gas Distribution System (NGS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Distribute and store argon as the cover gas for sodium-containing systems
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.15, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The NI Air and Gas Distribution System (NGS) primarily includes argon gas distribution and storage systems. The argon gas distribution and storage systems distribute argon as the cover gas for sodium containing systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.15) describes this purpose for NI Air and Gas Distribution System (NGS). The other options are purposes of NI normal lighting system, Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC), and NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Seismic Monitoring System (SMS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Monitor ground motion and structural response so personnel can promptly assess an earthquake's effects
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.16, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The SMS monitors the vibratory ground motion and resultant vibratory responses of representative structures so that plant personnel can take prompt action to assess the effects of an earthquake at the Kemmerer Unit 1 site."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.16) describes this purpose for Seismic Monitoring System (SMS). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting, Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC), and NI normal lighting system.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Scram the reactor before the peak seismic wave arrives in beyond-design-basis earthquakes
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.8.1, p. 7.6-75 (PDF page 1503)
  - Quote: "The AST is used during seismic beyond design basis events greater than the safe shutdown earthquake to scram the reactor before the peak seismic wave reaches the facility."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.6.8.1) describes this purpose for Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS), Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC), and Reactor Building (RXB).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Mitigate the effects of fire within and around the NI facilities
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.18, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 48)
  - Quote: "The primary purpose of the NI Fire Protection System (NFP) is to mitigate the effects of fire within and around the NI facilities."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.3.18) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP). The other options are purposes of NI DC Power Supply System (NDC), Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH), and Reactor Core System (RCC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Distribute fire water for hydrants and water-based fire suppression
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD) distributes fire water for fire hydrants and water-based fire suppression within NI buildings, facilities, structures, and yard area."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.5.2.1) describes this purpose for NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD). The other options are purposes of Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC), NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV), and Nuclear Island Auxiliary Electrical Systems.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Suppression System (NFS) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Suppress and control fire with water, clean agents and chemical means
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Suppression System (NFS) suppresses and controls fire with water, clean agents, and chemical means in both automatic systems and manual fire-fighting methods."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.5.2.1) describes this purpose for NI Fire Suppression System (NFS). The other options are purposes of Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC), Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS), and Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Detect smoke and fire, monitor and control suppression systems, and notify personnel
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA) detects smoke and fire, monitors and controls suppression systems, and notifies personnel of fire emergency situations."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.5.2.1) describes this purpose for NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting, Reactor Building (RXB), and NI DC Power Supply System (NDC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. Detect, collect and contain sodium leaks to mitigate sodium fires
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA) detects, collects, and contains sodium leaks to mitigate sodium fires."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 7.5.2.1) describes this purpose for Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA). The other options are purposes of Guard Vessel (GV), Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG), and Reactor Enclosure System (RES).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Building (RXB) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. House the reactor and the associated SSCs that support reactor operation
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.2, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 48)
  - Quote: "The RXB is the center point of the NI and houses the reactor and associated SSCs that support reactor operation."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.2) describes this purpose for Reactor Building (RXB). The other options are purposes of Reactor Protection System (RPS), Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC), and NI normal lighting system.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Handling Building (FHB) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: D. House fuel receipt, refueling, storage and the spent fuel pool, plus radwaste equipment
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.3, p. 1.1-19 (PDF page 49)
  - Quote: "The FHB houses plant operations and equipment related to fuel receipt, refueling operations, storage, and the SFP, along with equipment associated with the RWL, RWG, and RWS systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.3) describes this purpose for Fuel Handling Building (FHB). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH), Reactor Enclosure System (RES), and Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. House functions and processes that support the IHT, SHXs, ISPs and SPS
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.4, p. 1.1-19 (PDF page 49)
  - Quote: "The RAB is comprised of two reinforced concrete substructure levels and a steel-framed superstructure that houses critical functions and processes that support the IHT, SHXs, ISPs, and SPS."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.4) describes this purpose for Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB), Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG), and Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: A. Serve as the primary control center for the NI, housing the MCR
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.5, p. 1.1-20 (PDF page 50)
  - Quote: "The NCB serves as the primary control center for the NI that houses the MCR and associated equipment to ensure safe plant operations."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.5) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB). The other options are purposes of Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST), Radiation Monitoring System (RMS), and Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB) as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: C. Provide the centralized personnel entry and exit point for the major NI facilities
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.6, p. 1.1-20 (PDF page 50)
  - Quote: "The Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB) is a steel-braced frame structure supported on a concrete grade slab that provides a centralized location for employee and visitor ingress to, and egress from the major NI facilities (RXB, FHB, RAB)."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.6) describes this purpose for Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB). The other options are purposes of Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH), Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC), and Nuclear Island Distributed Control System (DCS).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Nuclear Island systems): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island E-Modules as described in the PSAR?
  - Answer: B. Contain NI electrical systems and components in prefabricated modules
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.8, p. 1.1-21 (PDF page 51)
  - Quote: "Prefabricated E-Modules are located on the NI area to contain electrical systems and components of the electrical systems."
  - Why: The PSAR (Sec. 1.1.4.4.8) describes this purpose for Nuclear Island E-Modules. The other options are purposes of Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST), Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG), and Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC).
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): According to the PSAR, which functions does the Reactor Enclosure System (RES) provide during normal and off-normal conditions?
  - Answer: D. Radionuclide retention, reactivity control, and reactor heat removal
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1, p. 7.1-14 (PDF page 1211)
  - Quote: "The RES provides radionuclide retention, reactivity control, and reactor heat removal functions during normal and off-normal conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR states the RES provides radionuclide retention, reactivity control, and reactor heat removal functions.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): Together with the PHT and the RES, the Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC) provides which function?
  - Answer: C. The long-term emergency core cooling function
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.2.1.1, p. 7.2-1 (PDF page 1280)
  - Quote: "The RAC, in conjunction with the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT) (Section 7.1.3) and the Reactor Enclosure System (RES) (Section 7.1.2), provides the long-term emergency core cooling function."
  - Why: The PSAR says the RAC, in conjunction with the PHT and RES, provides the long-term emergency core cooling function.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): What actuation does the Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC) need to perform its heat removal safety function?
  - Answer: B. None; it is continuously in operation with no automatic or manual actuation or operator action
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.2.1.1, p. 7.2-1 (PDF page 1280)
  - Quote: "The RAC is continuously in operation and requires no automatic or manual actuations or operator action to perform the heat removal safety function."
  - Why: The RAC is continuously in operation and requires no automatic or manual actuations or operator action.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): During a design basis event, how does the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT) support decay heat removal?
  - Answer: A. It facilitates natural circulation of primary sodium to carry heat to the reactor vessel walls, then to the guard vessel and the RAC
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.4, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "During a design basis event, the PHT safety function is to facilitate natural circulation of the primary sodium to transfer heat from the reactor core to the reactor vessel walls, where the heat is exchanged to the guard vessel and to the RAC."
  - Why: The PSAR states the PHT safety function during a DBE is to facilitate natural circulation to the vessel walls, where heat passes to the guard vessel and the RAC.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): If pumped flow is lost, how does the Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT) support decay heat removal?
  - Answer: C. Natural circulation of intermediate sodium through the IAC sodium-air heat exchangers
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.4.1, p. 7.1-72 (PDF page 1269)
  - Quote: "In the event of a loss of pumped flow, the IHT is designed to provide natural circulation of intermediate coolant for reactor decay heat removal through the IAC Sodium-Air Heat Exchangers (AHXs)."
  - Why: The PSAR states the IHT is designed to provide natural circulation of intermediate coolant for decay heat removal through the IAC AHXs.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): According to the PSAR, what is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions?
  - Answer: D. The Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC)
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.2.2.1, p. 7.2-13 (PDF page 1292)
  - Quote: "The IAC is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR names the IAC as the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown; the RAC provides passive long-term emergency core cooling.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Reactivity): Which system controls the Control Rod Drive System (CRD) scram function?
  - Answer: A. The Reactor Protection System (RPS)
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.9, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The scram function is controlled by the RPS."
  - Why: The PSAR states the CRD scram function is controlled by the RPS.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Reactivity): Why must the Reactor Core System (RCC) maintain its geometry during postulated accidents?
  - Answer: A. To support the natural circulation flowpath through the core and allow control rod insertion for shutdown
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.1.2, p. 7.1-6 (PDF page 1203)
  - Quote: "the RCC is designed to maintain its geometry to support the natural circulation flowpath of primary coolant through the reactor core during postulated accidents and to allow for control rod insertion for reactor shutdown during postulated accident conditions."
  - Why: The PSAR states the RCC is designed to maintain its geometry to support natural circulation and to allow control rod insertion during postulated accidents.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Reactivity): How does the Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST) scram the reactor?
  - Answer: B. It sends actuation signals to the Reactor Trip Breakers through an interface device provided by the RPS
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.8.1, p. 7.6-75 (PDF page 1503)
  - Quote: "automatically generates output actuation signals to the Reactor Trip Breakers (RTBs) through the interface device provided by the Reactor Protection System (RPS) when required by seismic conditions."
  - Why: The AST generates output actuation signals to the Reactor Trip Breakers through the interface device provided by the RPS.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Instrumentation): Where does the Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS) send its conditioned neutron flux signals?
  - Answer: A. To the RPS and the NIC, for protective, control and monitoring functions
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.12, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The XIS amplifies and conditions the instrument signals and provides corresponding input signals to the RPS and the NI Control System (NIC) for use in protective, control, and monitoring functions."
  - Why: The XIS provides input signals to the RPS and the NIC for use in protective, control, and monitoring functions.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Instrumentation): Which leak detection parameters does the Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS) provide to the RPS?
  - Answer: D. Reactor vessel to guard vessel annulus liquid sodium leak detection
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.14, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "RIS also provides the RV-GV annulus liquid sodium leak detection parameters as an input to RPS."
  - Why: The PSAR states the RIS provides the RV-GV annulus liquid sodium leak detection parameters as an input to the RPS.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Instrumentation): Which Radiation Monitoring System subsystem gives operators early indication of abnormal radiological conditions in a process, such as failed fuel?
  - Answer: B. Process radiation monitoring
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The process radiation monitoring subsystem strategy is to give operators early indication of abnormal radiological conditions in a plant process that may be an indication of failures within, or external to, the monitored process (e.g., failed fuel detection)."
  - Why: Area monitoring warns personnel of radiation hazards, effluent monitoring protects the public at release points, and process monitoring gives early indication of process failures such as failed fuel.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Instrumentation): What is the primary function of the RMS effluent radiation monitoring subsystem?
  - Answer: C. Protect public health and safety and assure off-site exposure stays within 10 CFR 20 limits
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The effluent radiation monitoring subsystem’s primary function is to protect the health and safety of the public and to provide assurance that off-site exposure does not exceed 10 CFR 20 limits."
  - Why: The PSAR states the effluent subsystem's primary function is to protect the public and assure off-site exposure does not exceed 10 CFR 20 limits.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): Why is the annulus between the reactor vessel and guard vessel inerted with argon?
  - Answer: C. To minimize the potential for sodium-air reaction
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1.3, p. 7.1-17 (PDF page 1214)
  - Quote: "The annular space is inerted with argon gas minimizing the potential for sodium-air reaction."
  - Why: The PSAR states the RV-GV annular space is inerted with argon, minimizing the potential for sodium-air reaction.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): What does transferring core assemblies in a shielded and inert environment provide in the Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System?
  - Answer: D. Radiation shielding, radionuclide retention, and a medium for removal of decay heat
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1, p. 7.3-16 (PDF page 1365)
  - Quote: "Transfer of core assemblies in a shielded and inert environment provides radiation shielding, radionuclide retention, and a medium for removal of decay heat."
  - Why: The PSAR lists radiation shielding, radionuclide retention, and a medium for removal of decay heat.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): Which functions does the Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP) provide for stored fuel?
  - Answer: B. Core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.1.1, p. 7.3-1 (PDF page 1350)
  - Quote: "The FHP provides core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding."
  - Why: The PSAR states the FHP provides core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): Which fundamental safety function does the Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG) support?
  - Answer: A. Retaining radionuclides
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.4.1.1, p. 7.4-1 (PDF page 1401)
  - Quote: "The RWG is classified as NSRST because it supports the retain radionuclides fundamental safety function, which protects plant personnel and the environment, supports compliance with 10 CFR Part 20, and minimizes radioactive releases."
  - Why: The RWG is classified NSRST because it supports the retain radionuclides fundamental safety function.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Decay heat): How does the Reactor Building substructure support decay heat removal during design basis accidents?
  - Answer: A. It supports and protects the RES and RAC so the geometry for passive residual heat removal is maintained
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.1.1.2, p. 7.8-3 (PDF page 1521)
  - Quote: "the RXB substructure is designed to structurally support and protect the RES and RAC such that the geometry for passive removal of residual heat from the reactor core is maintained during DBAs."
  - Why: The PSAR states the RXB substructure structurally supports and protects the RES and RAC so the geometry for passive removal of residual heat is maintained during DBAs.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): What radionuclide retention role does the Reactor Auxiliary Building substructure have?
  - Answer: C. It provides an enveloping boundary for radionuclide retention in the SPS cells
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.3.1.2, p. 7.8-19 (PDF page 1537)
  - Quote: "The RAB substructure provides an enveloping boundary for radionuclide retention in the SPS cells."
  - Why: The PSAR lists DL4-RR3, SPS Cells Barrier: the RAB substructure provides an enveloping boundary for radionuclide retention in the SPS cells.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Safety functions): In which building does the Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV) provide a radionuclide retention function as part of the PRA defense line level four functions?
  - Answer: C. The Reactor Building (RXB)
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.10, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "NHV provides a radionuclide retention function as part of the PRA defense line level four functions in the RXB."
  - Why: The PSAR states the NHV provides a radionuclide retention function as part of the PRA defense line level four functions in the RXB.
- **Quiz** (PSAR design basis; Reactivity): Which CRD function does the NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP) power through the control rod drive motor controllers?
  - Answer: D. The scram follow motor drive-in function
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.1, p. 7.7-1 (PDF page 1509)
  - Quote: "Control rod drive motor controllers (for scram follow motor drive-in function)"
  - Why: The NUP list of loads includes control rod drive motor controllers for the scram follow motor drive-in function.

## 2026-11-02: LP-ALIP-PUMPS (ALIP Pumps)

Approved lesson plan: ALIP Pumps.docx. Quotes are from the slide notes and on-slide text extracted with python-docx (RTF notes chunks converted with textutil); the section is the slide number and heading.

- **Card** (Pumps): What is an annular linear induction pump (ALIP)?
  - Answer: An electromagnetic pump that moves liquid without impellers or rotating shafts. It uses electromagnetic induction to propel the liquid through a circular channel.
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.1 ALIP Intro
  - Quote: "Annular Linear Induction Pumps are a type of electromagnetic pump used to move liquids without the need for any physical parts like impellers or rotating shafts. Instead, it utilizes the principles of electromagnetic induction to propel the liquid through a circular channel."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Quiz** (Pumps): In an annular linear induction pump, what acts as the current-carrying conductor in the magnetic field?
  - Answer: B. The liquid metal in the flow channel
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.3 ALIP Parts
  - Quote: "In the flow channel, the liquid metal acts as the ”current carrying conductor in the magnetic field” which allows the liquid metal to move through the pump at speeds dictated by the strength and speed of the magnetic field movement."
  - Why: The lesson plan says the liquid metal in the flow channel acts as the current-carrying conductor in the magnetic field, which moves it through the pump.
- **Card** (Pumps): Why does an ALIP with stator windings on both sides of the channel need an inner core?
  - Answer: A solid conductive inner core bridges the gap to maintain a strong magnetic field in the channel.
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.3 ALIP Parts
  - Quote: "Note that since this design has stator windings on both sides of the channel an inner core of solid conductive material is needed to bridge the gap to maintain a strong magnetic field in the channel."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Quiz** (Pumps): Which is an advantage of annular linear induction pumps compared with other pump types?
  - Answer: B. Lower net positive suction head requirements
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!
  - Quote: "They require lower Net Positive Suction Head requirements compared to other pump types."
  - Why: The lesson plan lists lower NPSH requirements as an advantage; lower flow for a given power input, lower net efficiency at higher flows, and harder stator heat removal are listed as disadvantages.
- **Card** (Pumps): What are the disadvantages of annular linear induction pumps?
  - Answer: Lower flow rates for a given power input, lower net efficiency at higher flows, and harder heat removal from the stator.
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!
  - Quote: "Some disadvantages are that their flow rates are lower for a Given Power Input which could be a drawback for high-flow applications. They can have lower Net Efficiency based on energy consumption for higher flows. Finally, they are harder to remove heat from the stator due to their design possibly requiring additional cooling or special materials."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Card** (Pumps): In an ALIP, what is the air gap power (Pgap)?
  - Answer: The amount of power transferred from the stator to the rotor. It is calculated from the applied power and the pump efficiency.
  - Source: LP-ALIP-PUMPS, slide 1.4 ALIP, How It Works!
  - Quote: "Air Gap, represented by Pgap, is the amount of power that is transferred FROM the Stator to the Rotor."
  - Quote: "In order to calculate Air Gap, we need to know what power is applied to the pump AND the pump efficiency."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.

## 2026-11-02: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS (Failed Fuel Detectors)

Approved lesson plan: Failed Fuel Detectors.docx. Quotes are from the slide notes and on-slide text extracted with python-docx (RTF notes chunks converted with textutil); the section is the slide number and heading.

- **Quiz** (Instrumentation): Why do radiation detectors contain a gas?
  - Answer: B. Ionized particles travel more freely in a gas than in a liquid or solid
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.4 Ion Chamber Nuclear Instruments
  - Quote: "Radiation detectors contain gases because their ionized particles can travel more freely than ionized particles of a liquid or a solid can."
  - Why: The lesson plan says detectors contain gases because ionized particles can travel more freely than in a liquid or a solid.
- **Card** (Instrumentation): Which fill gases do most radiation detectors use, and which gas do neutron detectors use?
  - Answer: Most use argon and helium. Detectors designed to measure neutrons use boron trifluoride.
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.4 Ion Chamber Nuclear Instruments
  - Quote: "Most detectors use argon and helium gas; detectors designed to measure neutrons use boron trifluoride."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Quiz** (Instrumentation): How does a boron trifluoride (BF3) proportional counter detect neutrons?
  - Answer: A. Neutrons react with boron atoms in the gas to produce alpha particles
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.5 BF3 Chamber
  - Quote: "The incoming neutrons produce alpha particles when they react with the boron atoms in the detector gas."
  - Why: Neutrons are not directly ionizing; in a BF3 counter they react with boron atoms to produce alpha particles, which are detected.
- **Card** (Instrumentation): What does a pulse-height discriminator do in a BF3 detector?
  - Answer: It sifts through the signals to determine which are generated by neutrons and which by other interactions.
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.5 BF3 Chamber
  - Quote: "With a Pulse-Height Discriminator, we can sift through all the signals and determine which signals are generated by neutrons, and which signals are generated by other interactions."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Quiz** (Instrumentation): Why does a fission chamber produce a large pulse for neutrons compared with gamma?
  - Answer: B. Neutron-induced fission in the U-235 coating creates high-energy fragments that cause many ionizations
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.6 U-235 Chamber
  - Quote: "In this case, the inner wall is coated with highly enriched Uranium-235, making this a Fission Chamber."
  - Quote: "These highly charged particles interact with the fill gas, usually Argon, to produce many ionizations thus creating a large pulse from neutron-induced fission when compared to gamma pulses."
  - Why: The inner wall is coated with highly enriched U-235; fission fragments interact with the fill gas to produce many ionizations and a large pulse compared with gamma pulses.
- **Card** (Instrumentation): How does loss of voltage affect a radiation or neutron detector?
  - Answer: It fails the detector low. Other circuitry issues can fail it low or high, depending on the malfunction.
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.7 Malfunctions
  - Quote: "Loss of voltage will fail the detector low while circuitry issues may fail the detector Low, or High, depending on the malfunction."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
- **Card** (Instrumentation): Why do BF3 detectors eventually have to be replaced?
  - Answer: The boron trifluoride fill gas burns out over time.
  - Source: LP-FAILED-FUEL-DETECTORS, slide 1.7 Malfunctions
  - Quote: "Boron Tri-Fluoride fill-gas will burn out over time causing the detector to be replaced."
  - Why: The answer restates the quoted text.
