- **C483** (Controllers and Positioners): What are the three types of logic time delay devices?
  - Source: DOE-1016-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1016/2-93), Engineering Logic Diagrams, PR-05 p. 10 (PDF page 60)
  - Quote: "There are three types of time delay devices: Type One - delays the output signal for a specified period of time Type Two - only generates an output for the specified period of time Type Three - receipt of an input signal triggers the device to output a signal for the specified time, regardless of the duration of the input"
- **C484** (Controllers and Positioners): How many basic symbols are used on logic diagrams?
  - Source: DOE-1016-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1016/2-93), Engineering Logic Diagrams, PR-05 p. 10 (PDF page 60)
  - Quote: "This chapter reviewed the seven basic symbols used on logic diagrams"
  - Figure: images/doe-1016-v2-pr-05-fig3.png
- **Q453** (Controllers and Positioners): In logic gate status notation, what does the first part of the square wave indicate?
  - Source: DOE-1016-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1016/2-93), Truth Tables and Exercises, PR-05 p. 13 (PDF page 63)
  - Quote: "The first part of the square wave indicates the normal state of the gate."
- **Q454** (Controllers and Positioners): Which time delay device only generates an output for the specified period of time?
  - Source: DOE-1016-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1016/2-93), Engineering Logic Diagrams, PR-05 p. 10 (PDF page 60)
  - Quote: "Type Two - only generates an output for the specified period of time"
- **Q455** (Controllers and Positioners): For a Type Three time delay device, how long does the output last?
  - Source: DOE-1016-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1016/2-93), Engineering Logic Diagrams, PR-05 p. 10 (PDF page 60)
  - Quote: "Type Three - receipt of an input signal triggers the device to output a signal for the specified time, regardless of the duration of the input"

### Figures

## 2026-11-04: DOE-1012-V1 (Thermodynamics, Heat Transfer and Fluid Flow, Vol 1)

Added 11 quiz questions and 12 flashcards. Every quote was matched against work/text/DOE-HDBK-1012-92_VOL1.txt.

- **C485** (Steam): What is saturation?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Saturation - combination of temperature and pressure at which a mixture of vapor and liquid can exist at equilibrium"
- **C486** (Steam): What is a subcooled liquid?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Subcooled liquid - a liquid at a temperature below saturation temperature for its pressure"
- **C487** (Steam): What is a superheated vapor?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Superheated vapor - a vapor at a temperature above saturation temperature for its pressure"
- **C488** (Steam): What is the critical point?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Critical point - the temperature and pressure above which there is no distinction between the liquid and vapor phases"
  - Figure: images/doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig13.png
- **C489** (Steam): What is the triple point?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Triple point - the temperature and pressure at which all three phases can exist in equilibrium"
- **C490** (Steam): What is quality?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Quality - the fraction of the total mass of a mixture that is in the vapor phase"
- **C491** (Steam): What is moisture content?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Moisture Content - the fraction of the total mass of a mixture that is in the liquid phase"
- **C492** (Steam): What does a Mollier diagram plot?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Property Diagrams and Steam Tables, HT-01 p. 52 (PDF page 78)
  - Quote: "Mollier diagram is an h versus s plot."
- **Q456** (Steam): A Mollier diagram can only be used for superheated steam and when quality is:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Property Diagrams and Steam Tables, HT-01 p. 52 (PDF page 78)
  - Quote: "Can only be used when quality is greater than 50% and for superheated steam."
- **Q457** (Steam): A vapor pressure curve shows the relationship between temperature and pressure at:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Vapor pressure curve - a graphical representation of the relationship between temperature and pressure at saturated conditions"
- **Q458** (Steam): Water at a temperature below saturation temperature for its pressure is:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Subcooled liquid - a liquid at a temperature below saturation temperature for its pressure"
- **Q459** (Steam): Steam quality is the fraction of a mixture's total mass that is:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Quality - the fraction of the total mass of a mixture that is in the vapor phase"
- **Q460** (Steam): Which equation gives the specific enthalpy of a saturated mixture with quality x?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Property Diagrams and Steam Tables, HT-01 p. 44 (PDF page 70)
  - Quote: "h = xhg + (1 - x)hf"
- **Q461** (Steam): Above which point is there no distinction between the liquid and vapor phases?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Change of Phase, HT-01 p. 39 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Critical point - the temperature and pressure above which there is no distinction between the liquid and vapor phases"
  - Figure: images/doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig13.png
- **C493** (Thermodynamic Cycles): What four processes make up the Rankine cycle?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 61 (PDF page 87)
  - Quote: "ab: Liquid is compressed with no change in entropy (by ideal pump). bc: Constant pressure transfer of heat in the boiler. Heat is added to the compressed liquid, two-phase, and superheat states. cd: Constant entropy expansion with shaft work output (in ideal turbine). da: Constant pressure transfer of heat in the sink. Unavailable heat is rejected to the heat sink (condenser)."
  - Figure: images/doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig19.png
- **C494** (Thermodynamic Cycles): What is a cyclic process?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 61 (PDF page 87)
  - Quote: "If the fluid passes through various processes and then eventually returns to the same state it began with, the system is said to have undergone a cyclic process."
- **C495** (Thermodynamic Cycles): What is the heat-rejection mechanism of a steam plant cycle?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 62 (PDF page 88)
  - Quote: "The condensation process is the heat-rejection mechanism for the cycle."
- **C496** (Thermodynamic Cycles): What decreases cycle efficiency?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Second Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 96 (PDF page 122)
  - Quote: "Efficiency will be decreased by: Presence of friction Heat losses Cycle inefficiencies"
- **Q462** (Thermodynamic Cycles): How can the maximum efficiency of a closed cycle be determined?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Second Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 96 (PDF page 122)
  - Quote: "The maximum efficiency of a closed cycle can be determined by calculating the efficiency of a Carnot cycle operating between the same value of high and low temperatures."
- **Q463** (Thermodynamic Cycles): A cycle operates between 1,000 °R and 600 °R. What is its Carnot efficiency?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), Second Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 96 (PDF page 122)
  - Quote: "η = (TH - TC)/TH"
- **Q464** (Thermodynamic Cycles): In the Rankine cycles shown, the ideal turbine expansion from c to d occurs at constant:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 61 (PDF page 87)
  - Quote: "cd: Constant entropy expansion with shaft work output (in ideal turbine)."
  - Figure: images/doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig19.png
- **Q465** (Thermodynamic Cycles): In a Rankine cycle, heat transfer in the boiler occurs at constant:
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 61 (PDF page 87)
  - Quote: "bc: Constant pressure transfer of heat in the boiler."
- **Q466** (Thermodynamic Cycles): In a typical steam plant cycle, where does vapor go after leaving the turbine?
  - Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), First Law of Thermodynamics, HT-01 p. 62 (PDF page 88)
  - Quote: "Vapor leaving the turbine then enters the condenser where heat is removed and the vapor is condensed into the liquid state."

### Figures

- **doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig13.png** (41 KB, in flashcards and quiz): Figure 13. T-s Diagram for Water. Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), HT-01 p. 46. PDF page 72. Alt text: Temperature-entropy diagram for water. A dome peaks at the critical point, with the liquid region on the left, the vapor region on the right, the liquid-vapor region under the dome, and the solid-vapor region at the bottom. Constant pressure lines P1 to P4 are shown.
- **doe-1012-v1-ht-01-fig19.png** (41 KB, in flashcards and quiz): Figure 19. T-s Diagram with Rankine Cycles. Source: DOE-1012-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1012/1-92), HT-01 p. 61. PDF page 87. Alt text: Two temperature-entropy diagrams of a Rankine cycle with points a, b, c, and d around the saturation dome and the rejected heat shaded below the cycle. The upper cycle reaches superheat at point c; the lower one does not.

## 2026-11-04: DOE-1019-V2 (Nuclear Physics and Reactor Theory, Vol 2)

Added 11 quiz questions and 10 flashcards. Every quote was matched against work/text/DOE-HDBK-1019-93_VOL2.txt.

- **C497** (Fission Product Poisons): How is xenon-135 produced during reactor operation?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 41 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Xenon-135 is produced directly as a fission product and by the decay of iodine-135 during reactor operation."
- **C498** (Fission Product Poisons): How is xenon-135 removed from the core during reactor operation?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 41 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "Xenon-135 is removed from the core by radioactive decay and by neutron absorption during reactor operation."
- **C499** (Fission Product Poisons): What is a xenon precluded startup?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "A xenon precluded startup occurs when there is insufficient reactivity in the control rods to overcome the negative reactivity of xenon-135."
- **C500** (Fission Product Poisons): What is xenon dead time?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "Xenon dead time is the period of time where the reactor is unable to override the effects of xenon."
- **C501** (Fission Product Poisons): What may cause a xenon-135 oscillation?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "A xenon-135 oscillation may be caused by a rapid perturbation in the core power distribution."
- **C502** (Fission Product Poisons): How is samarium-149 produced during reactor operation?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "Samarium-149 is produced directly from fission and from the decay of promethium-149 during reactor operation."
- **C503** (Fission Product Poisons): How does equilibrium samarium-149 concentration depend on power level?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "The equilibrium samarium-149 concentration is independent of power level."
  - Figure: images/doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig7.png
- **C504** (Fission Product Poisons): When does helium-3 become a significant neutron poison?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "Helium-3 will become a significant neutron poison if significant amounts of tritium are left in a reactor during a shutdown period that lasts longer than several months."
- **Q467** (Fission Product Poisons): After a shutdown from 100% power, xenon-135 peaks approximately how long after shutdown?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "Xenon-135 will peak approximately 10 hours after the shutdown (from 100%)"
  - Figure: images/doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig5.png
- **Q468** (Fission Product Poisons): About how long after shutdown can the core be considered xenon-free?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "The core can be considered xenon-free about 3 days after shutdown."
- **Q469** (Fission Product Poisons): What does xenon-135 concentration initially do after a power increase, and why?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 41 (PDF page 65)
  - Quote: "After a power increase, xenon-135 concentration will initially decrease due to the increased removal by burnout."
- **Q470** (Fission Product Poisons): What does xenon-135 concentration initially do after a power decrease, and why?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "After a power decrease, xenon-135 concentration will initially increase due to production by iodine decay being greater than the burnout."
- **Q471** (Fission Product Poisons): In the curves shown, what sets the size of the xenon peak after shutdown?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Xenon, NP-03 p. 42 (PDF page 66)
  - Quote: "The greater the pre-shutdown power level, the greater the peak value of xenon."
  - Figure: images/doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig5.png
- **Q472** (Fission Product Poisons): In the figure, why does samarium-149 reactivity grow during the shutdown?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "Following a reactor shutdown, the samarium-149 concentration increases due to the decay of the promethium-149 inventory of the core and the loss of the burnup factor."
  - Figure: images/doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig7.png
- **Q473** (Fission Product Poisons): After a restart, what happens to samarium-149 concentration?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "If the reactor is restarted following a shutdown, the samarium-149 concentration decreases as samarium is burned up and returns to its equilibrium operating value."
- **Q474** (Fission Product Poisons): How is samarium-149 removed from the core?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Samarium and Other Fission Product Poisons, NP-03 p. 47 (PDF page 71)
  - Quote: "Samarium-149 is removed from the core by neutron absorption."
- **C505** (Fuel Depletion and Burnable Poisons): What is a burnable neutron poison?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Neutron Poisons, NP-03 p. 33 (PDF page 57)
  - Quote: "A burnable neutron poison is a material that has a high neutron absorption cross section that is converted into a material of relatively low absorption cross section as the result of neutron absorption."
- **C506** (Fuel Depletion and Burnable Poisons): What is chemical shim?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Neutron Poisons, NP-03 p. 33 (PDF page 57)
  - Quote: "Chemical shim is a soluble neutron poison that is circulated in the coolant during normal operation."
- **Q475** (Fuel Depletion and Burnable Poisons): Why are burnable neutron poisons used in reactor cores?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Neutron Poisons, NP-03 p. 33 (PDF page 57)
  - Quote: "Burnable neutron poisons are used in reactor cores to compensate for the excess positive reactivity of the fuel when the reactor is initially started up."
- **Q476** (Fuel Depletion and Burnable Poisons): Which is an advantage of fixed burnable poisons over chemical shim?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Neutron Poisons, NP-03 p. 33 (PDF page 57)
  - Quote: "Fixed burnable poisons have several advantages over chemical shim. Can be used to shape flux profiles Do not have an adverse effect on moderator temperature coefficient"
- **Q477** (Fuel Depletion and Burnable Poisons): Which material is an example of a fixed non-burnable neutron poison?
  - Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), Neutron Poisons, NP-03 p. 33 (PDF page 57)
  - Quote: "An example of a material that is used as a fixed non-burnable neutron poison is hafnium."

### Figures

- **doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig7.png** (37 KB, in flashcards and quiz): Figure 7. Behavior of Samarium-149 in a Typical Light Water Reactor. Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), NP-03 p. 46. PDF page 70. Alt text: Graph of samarium negative reactivity against time in days. Reactivity rises to an equilibrium value during initial operation at 100 percent, rises further during shutdown from day 20 to 35, then falls back to the same equilibrium value after restart.
- **doe-1019-v2-np-03-fig5.png** (69 KB, in quiz): Figure 5. Xenon-135 Reactivity After Reactor Shutdown. Source: DOE-1019-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1019/2-93), NP-03 p. 38. PDF page 62. Alt text: Graph of negative reactivity against time after shutdown, from 0 to 70 hours, for four pre-shutdown flux levels. The three higher-flux curves rise to a peak near 10 hours and then fall, with higher pre-shutdown flux giving much higher peaks. The lowest-flux curve only falls.

## 2026-11-04: PSAR Nuclear Island flashcards

At the user's request, added 82 flashcards from the Nuclear Island quiz questions (Q153 to Q235), using each question's correct option as the answer. Purpose cards drop "as described in the PSAR" from the stem. Each quote was re-matched against work/text/ML24088A065.txt on its logged page. Q217 was left out because card C140 already covers it. The quiz questions are unchanged.

- **C507** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q153): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Core System (RCC)?
  - Answer: Sustain a nuclear chain reaction for fission heat generation.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.1, p. 1.1-3 (PDF page 33)
  - Quote: "The RCC is designed to sustain a nuclear chain reaction for fission heat generation within the thermal-mechanical constraints of the components (e.g., fuel, cladding, structures)."
- **C508** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q154): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Enclosure System (RES)?
  - Answer: Support the reactor core and contain the primary sodium coolant.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.2, p. 1.1-3 (PDF page 33)
  - Quote: "The RES supports the reactor core and contains the primary sodium coolant."
- **C509** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q155): What is the primary purpose of the Guard Vessel (GV)?
  - Answer: Provide a defense-in-depth coolant and functional containment boundary if the reactor vessel leaks.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1.3, p. 7.1-16 (PDF page 1213)
  - Quote: "The RV is surrounded by a GV, which provides a defense-in-depth coolant and functional containment boundary in the unlikely occurrence of RV leakage."
- **C510** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q156): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC)?
  - Answer: Provide passive decay heat removal to the environment by natural convection of air.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.3, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The RAC primary objective is to provide passive decay heat removal to the environment through natural convection of air."
- **C511** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q157): What is the primary purpose of the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT)?
  - Answer: Transport heat from the reactor core to the Intermediate Heat Transport System.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.4, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The principal function of the PHT is to transport heat from the reactor core to the IHT for use in power generation."
- **C512** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q158): What is the primary purpose of the Primary Sodium Pumps (PSPs)?
  - Answer: Provide the head to drive primary sodium flow.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.3.2.1, p. 7.1-57 (PDF page 1254)
  - Quote: "During normal operations, plant startup and shutdown, and during certain LBEs, the PSPs provide the necessary head to drive primary sodium flow."
- **C513** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q159): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Heat Exchangers (IHXs)?
  - Answer: Transfer heat from the primary sodium to the intermediate sodium.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.3.3.1, p. 7.1-59 (PDF page 1256)
  - Quote: "There are two IHXs in the PHT that transfer heat from the primary sodium of the PHT to the intermediate sodium of IHT"
- **C514** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q160): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT)?
  - Answer: Transport heat away from the PHT to the salt system or to the air coolers.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.5, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "The IHT primary function is to transport heat away from the PHT. The IHT delivers the heat removed from the PHT to the NSS for energy storage or electrical power generation, or to the IAC to be rejected as waste heat to the atmosphere."
- **C515** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q161): What is the primary purpose of the Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC)?
  - Answer: Transfer heat from the intermediate sodium loops to the atmosphere.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.6, p. 1.1-5 (PDF page 35)
  - Quote: "The IAC is the preferred heat removal system for the reactor during upset events. The IAC transfers heat from the IHT to the atmosphere."
- **C516** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q162): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Salt System (NSS)?
  - Answer: Remove heat from the IHT sodium-salt heat exchangers into the molten salt loop.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.2.1, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "Heat is removed from the IHT SHXs in the RAB by the NSS to ESS to TSS molten salt loop during reactor operation."
- **C517** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q163): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Cover Gas System (SCG)?
  - Answer: Control, monitor and supply inert argon gas to systems and components in the RXB, RAB and FHB.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.7, p. 1.1-5 (PDF page 35)
  - Quote: "The SCG controls, monitors, and supplies inert argon gas to various systems and components throughout the Reactor Building (RXB), Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB), and Fuel Handling Building (FHB)."
- **C518** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q164): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Processing System (SPS)?
  - Answer: Monitor and remove contaminants such as cesium, oxygen and hydrogen from the liquid sodium.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.8, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The Sodium Processing System (SPS) monitors and removes contaminants including cesium and compounds including oxygen and hydrogen from the liquid sodium inventory."
- **C519** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q165): What is the primary purpose of the Control Rod Drive System (CRD)?
  - Answer: Provide core reactivity control for power control, power shaping and reactor shutdown.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.9, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The purpose of the CRD is to provide core reactivity control for the purpose of core power control, power shaping, and reactor shutdown."
- **C520** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q166): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Protection System (RPS)?
  - Answer: Automatically generate output signals to initiate reactor scram and engineered safety feature functions.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.11, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The primary function of the RPS is to, with precision and reliability, accept input signals from plant instrumentation, apply necessary logic, and automatically generate output signals to initiate safety functions including reactor scram and engineered safety feature functions when required by plant conditions."
- **C521** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q167): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS)?
  - Answer: Sense neutron flux leakage from the core.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.12, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS) provides instrumentation to sense neutron flux leakage from the core during fuel movement, reactor startup, power operations, shutdown, and accident conditions."
- **C522** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q168): What is the primary purpose of the Radiation Monitoring System (RMS)?
  - Answer: Provide radiation activity indications for systems, buildings and release pathways to protect personnel and the environment.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The Radiation Monitoring System (RMS) provides radiation activity indications for systems, buildings, and release pathways throughout the plant at strategic interface points for use in the protection of plant personnel and the surrounding environment during all operating conditions."
- **C523** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q169): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS)?
  - Answer: Measure parameters such as hot pool level and temperature and send them to the RPS and NIC.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.14, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS) provides measurements for parameters and sends these signals in an appropriate format to RPS, and NIC, for control, safety functions, post-accident monitoring, and informational purposes."
- **C524** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q170): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Control System (NIC)?
  - Answer: Group the non-safety I&C subsystems (RMC, CTC, UMC, AMC, FHC, PMC) that control the Nuclear Island.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.15, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The NIC is a group of I&C subsystems that perform non-safety-related with no special treatment (NST) and NSRST functions."
- **C525** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q171): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Distributed Control System (DCS)?
  - Answer: Gather information from field sensors, interfaces and other I&C systems as the primary NIC subsystem.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.5, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The DCS is the primary subsystem of the NIC and provides a means for gathering information from various sources, such as field sensors, human-system Interfaces (HSIs), and data feeds from other I&C systems."
- **C526** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q172): What is the primary purpose of the Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC)?
  - Answer: Control and monitor the primary and secondary control rod assemblies.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.16, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The Rod Monitoring and Control System (RMC) is a subsystem of the NIC that is used to control and monitor primary control rod assemblies and secondary control rod assemblies for all reactor operation modes."
- **C527** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q173): What is the primary purpose of the Coolant Temperature Monitoring and Control System (CTC)?
  - Answer: Monitor and control the flow control functions of the PHT, IHT, NSS, IAC and ESS.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.17, p. 1.1-9 (PDF page 39)
  - Quote: "The CTC monitors and controls the PHT, IHT, NSS, IAC, and EI Salt Heat Transport System (ESS) flow control functions."
- **C528** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q174): What is the primary purpose of the Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC)?
  - Answer: Monitor and control the auxiliary electrical and ancillary systems.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.2.1, p. 7.6-7 (PDF page 1435)
  - Quote: "Utility Monitoring and Control System (UMC) – The UMC monitors and controls the various auxiliary electrical and ancillary systems."
- **C529** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q175): What is the primary purpose of the Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC)?
  - Answer: Monitor and control Nuclear Island auxiliary systems such as radwaste, cover gas and sodium processing.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.2.1, p. 7.6-6 (PDF page 1434)
  - Quote: "Auxiliary Monitoring and Control System (AMC) – The AMC monitors and controls Nuclear Island (NI) auxiliary systems."
- **C530** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q176): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC)?
  - Answer: Serve as the supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) system for fuel handling.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.20, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "The Fuel Handling Supervisory Control System (FHC) functions as the Supervisory, Control and Data Acquisition (SCADA) for the fuel handling processes."
- **C531** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q177): What is the primary purpose of the Plant Monitoring and Control System (PMC)?
  - Answer: Let operators monitor plant data and manually control equipment through the HMI, with no automatic control.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.21, p. 1.1-10 (PDF page 40)
  - Quote: "The PMC provides plant operators the capability to monitor plant data and control plant equipment through the HMI in all operating modes. The PMC does not have ability to perform automatic control."
- **C532** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q178): What is the primary purpose of the In-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHI)?
  - Answer: Manipulate core assembly positions during refueling and maintain the primary functional containment boundary when installed.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.1, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "Together, these components manipulate the positions of core assemblies during refueling operations and maintain the primary functional containment boundary during all reactor modes when the equipment is installed."
- **C533** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q179): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHE)?
  - Answer: Facilitate the receipt, conditioning, storage, installation and removal of all core assemblies.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.2, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "The Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System (FHE) includes equipment that facilitates the receipt, conditioning, storage, installation, and removal of all core assemblies."
- **C534** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q180): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Handling Machine (EVHM)?
  - Answer: Transfer core assemblies in sodium-filled pots between the reactor vessel and the Ex-Vessel Storage Tank.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.1, p. 7.3-16 (PDF page 1365)
  - Quote: "It is used to transfer core assemblies (non-fuel, irradiated fuel, and non-irradiated fuel), contained within a liquid sodium filled core assembly pot (CAP), between the reactor vessel located in the Reactor Building (RXB) and the EVST located in the Fuel Handling Building (FHB)."
- **C535** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q181): What is the primary purpose of the Bottom Loading Transfer Cask (BLTC)?
  - Answer: Transfer core assemblies between the new assembly preconditioning station, the Pool Immersion Cell and the EVST.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.2, p. 7.3-18 (PDF page 1367)
  - Quote: "It is used to transfer core assemblies (non-fuel, irradiated fuel, and non-irradiated fuel), between the NAPS, Pool Immersion Cell and the EVST located in the FHB."
- **C536** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q182): What is the primary purpose of the Ex-Vessel Storage Tank (EVST)?
  - Answer: Provide a controlled sodium environment for temporary storage of new and irradiated core assemblies.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1.3, p. 7.3-19 (PDF page 1368)
  - Quote: "Its function is to provide a controlled environment for temporary storage for new components in route to the reactor, and irradiated core assemblies removed from the reactor."
- **C537** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q183): What is the primary purpose of the Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP)?
  - Answer: Store irradiated core assemblies in a water-cooled pool.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.3, p. 1.1-12 (PDF page 42)
  - Quote: "The Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP) consists of the subsystems and equipment necessary to store irradiated core assemblies within the water-cooled pool."
- **C538** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q184): What is the primary purpose of the Main Control Room (MCR)?
  - Answer: Let operators initiate or take manual control of each function needed to control the plant and maintain safety.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.4, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The MCR contains equipment that is part of the NIC that allows operators to initiate or take manual control of each function necessary to control the plant and maintain safety."
- **C539** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q185): What is the primary purpose of the Remote Shutdown Complex (RSC)?
  - Answer: Provide a location to monitor safe shutdown conditions if the MCR is no longer habitable.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.4.1.1, p. 7.8-27 (PDF page 1545)
  - Quote: "the NCB substructure includes a location for the RSC, as described in Section 7.6.7.2, that is used to monitor plant safe shutdown conditions in case the MCR is no longer habitable."
- **C540** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q186): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Auxiliary Electrical Systems?
  - Answer: Distribute auxiliary electrical power to the Nuclear Island.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NI electrical power distribution is divided into several systems to distribute auxiliary electrical power to the NI of Kemmerer Unit 1."
- **C541** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q187): What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV)?
  - Answer: Supply medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and the PSP and ISP adjustable speed drives.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NMV supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
- **C542** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q188): What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV)?
  - Answer: Supply 480V switchgear, motor control centers, switchboards and panelboards for NI auxiliary loads.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NLV supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
- **C543** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q189): What is the primary purpose of the NI Heat Tracing System (NHT)?
  - Answer: Power heating cables on process lines and tanks to prevent freezing and crystallization of fluids such as sodium and molten salt.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The NI electrical system also includes an NHT that distributes power to heating cables on process lines and tanks to maintain specific fluid temperature to prevent freezing and crystallization of process fluids, such as molten salts, sodium, and water."
- **C544** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q190): What is the primary purpose of the NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP)?
  - Answer: Provide uninterruptible AC power to NI loads such as the RPS, XIS, RMS and CRD motor controllers.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.1, p. 7.7-1 (PDF page 1509)
  - Quote: "The NUP provides uninterruptible AC power to NI loads, including the following:"
- **C545** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q191): What is the primary purpose of the NI DC Power Supply System (NDC)?
  - Answer: Provide continuous, stable DC power through four independent 250 VDC divisions, one per RPS division.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.3.2, p. 7.7-5 (PDF page 1513)
  - Quote: "For system reliability and to ensure continuous and stable uninterrupted electrical power is provided to NI systems and components, the NDC comprises four independent 250 VDC divisions - one for each Reactor Protection System division"
- **C546** (PSAR: Radwaste Systems, from Q192): What is the primary purpose of the Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG)?
  - Answer: Process cover gas waste streams and hold them up so radioactive isotopes such as argon-41 decay.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.7, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 43)
  - Quote: "The RWG is located in the FHB and is a once-through system that processes the gaseous waste streams from primary SCG and the SCG exhaust distribution cabinet. The system provides holdup for the decay of short-lived radioactive isotopes such as Argon-41."
- **C547** (PSAR: Radwaste Systems, from Q193): What is the primary purpose of the Liquid Radwaste Processing System (RWL)?
  - Answer: Collect, segregate, process, sample and monitor non-sodium, non-salt liquid radioactive waste.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.8, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The RWL is designed to collect, segregate, process, sample, and monitor the non-sodium and non-salt liquid radioactive waste for reuse or evaporation."
- **C548** (PSAR: Radwaste Systems, from Q194): What is the primary purpose of the Solid Radwaste Processing System (RWS)?
  - Answer: Process wet and dry solid waste from plant systems.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.9, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The RWS is designed to process both wet and dry solid waste from plant systems and sources."
- **C549** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q195): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV)?
  - Answer: Provide HVAC for personnel comfort, freeze protection and equipment operability.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.10, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "The NHV is provided as required for personnel comfort, freeze protection, and equipment operability in areas identified as requiring temperature control on a per-building basis."
- **C550** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q196): What is the primary purpose of the NI normal lighting system?
  - Answer: Provide general indoor and outdoor lighting during operation, maintenance and testing.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.11, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The normal lighting system provides illumination for general indoor and outdoor lighting during plant operation, maintenance, and test conditions."
- **C551** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q197): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Emergency Operating Lighting?
  - Answer: Provide illumination in NI plant areas during a station blackout.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.17, p. 1.1-17 (PDF page 47)
  - Quote: "NI emergency operating lighting provides illumination in NI plant areas during an station blackout (SBO)"
- **C552** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q198): What is the primary purpose of the NI Grounding and Earthing and Lightning Protection (NGL)?
  - Answer: Protect personnel and equipment from transient over-voltages and provide a ground reference for instrument signals.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.11, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The NGL provides protection of plant personnel and equipment from the effect of transient over-voltages that can occur in electrical systems, voltage surges due to electrical faults or lightning strikes, and provides a proper ground reference for the instrumentation signals."
- **C553** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q199): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Plant Communication System?
  - Answer: Provide an independent means of onsite and offsite communication in all modes, including emergencies.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.12, p. 1.1-15 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "The NI communication system is designed to provide an independent means of effective onsite and offsite communication during all modes of plant operation, including during abnormal and emergency operating conditions."
- **C554** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q200): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Cranes and Hoists (NCH)?
  - Answer: Lift and move approved loads within NI buildings.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.13, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The NCH primary function is to lift and move approved loads within the NI buildings to support normal operations, maintenance, and other required activities."
- **C555** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q201): What is the primary purpose of the NI Air and Gas Distribution System (NGS)?
  - Answer: Distribute and store argon as the cover gas for sodium-containing systems.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.15, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The NI Air and Gas Distribution System (NGS) primarily includes argon gas distribution and storage systems. The argon gas distribution and storage systems distribute argon as the cover gas for sodium containing systems."
- **C556** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components, from Q202): What is the primary purpose of the Seismic Monitoring System (SMS)?
  - Answer: Monitor ground motion and structural response so personnel can promptly assess an earthquake's effects.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.16, p. 1.1-16 (PDF page 46)
  - Quote: "The SMS monitors the vibratory ground motion and resultant vibratory responses of representative structures so that plant personnel can take prompt action to assess the effects of an earthquake at the Kemmerer Unit 1 site."
- **C557** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q203): What is the primary purpose of the Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST)?
  - Answer: Scram the reactor before the peak seismic wave arrives in beyond-design-basis earthquakes.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.8.1, p. 7.6-75 (PDF page 1503)
  - Quote: "The AST is used during seismic beyond design basis events greater than the safe shutdown earthquake to scram the reactor before the peak seismic wave reaches the facility."
- **C558** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q204): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Fire Protection System (NFP)?
  - Answer: Mitigate the effects of fire within and around the NI facilities.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.18, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 48)
  - Quote: "The primary purpose of the NI Fire Protection System (NFP) is to mitigate the effects of fire within and around the NI facilities."
- **C559** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q205): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD)?
  - Answer: Distribute fire water for hydrants and water-based fire suppression.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Water Distribution System (NFD) distributes fire water for fire hydrants and water-based fire suppression within NI buildings, facilities, structures, and yard area."
- **C560** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q206): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Suppression System (NFS)?
  - Answer: Suppress and control fire with water, clean agents and chemical means.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Suppression System (NFS) suppresses and controls fire with water, clean agents, and chemical means in both automatic systems and manual fire-fighting methods."
- **C561** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q207): What is the primary purpose of the NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA)?
  - Answer: Detect smoke and fire, monitor and control suppression systems, and notify personnel.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The NI Fire Detection and Alarm System (NFA) detects smoke and fire, monitors and controls suppression systems, and notifies personnel of fire emergency situations."
- **C562** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q208): What is the primary purpose of the Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA)?
  - Answer: Detect, collect and contain sodium leaks to mitigate sodium fires.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.5.2.1, p. 7.5-10 (PDF page 1420)
  - Quote: "The Sodium Leak Detection, Collection, and Containment System (NNA) detects, collects, and contains sodium leaks to mitigate sodium fires."
- **C563** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q209): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Building (RXB)?
  - Answer: House the reactor and the associated SSCs that support reactor operation.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.2, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 48)
  - Quote: "The RXB is the center point of the NI and houses the reactor and associated SSCs that support reactor operation."
- **C564** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q210): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Handling Building (FHB)?
  - Answer: House fuel receipt, refueling, storage and the spent fuel pool, plus radwaste equipment.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.3, p. 1.1-19 (PDF page 49)
  - Quote: "The FHB houses plant operations and equipment related to fuel receipt, refueling operations, storage, and the SFP, along with equipment associated with the RWL, RWG, and RWS systems."
- **C565** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q211): What is the primary purpose of the Reactor Auxiliary Building (RAB)?
  - Answer: House functions and processes that support the IHT, SHXs, ISPs and SPS.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.4, p. 1.1-19 (PDF page 49)
  - Quote: "The RAB is comprised of two reinforced concrete substructure levels and a steel-framed superstructure that houses critical functions and processes that support the IHT, SHXs, ISPs, and SPS."
- **C566** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q212): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Control Building (NCB)?
  - Answer: Serve as the primary control center for the NI, housing the MCR.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.5, p. 1.1-20 (PDF page 50)
  - Quote: "The NCB serves as the primary control center for the NI that houses the MCR and associated equipment to ensure safe plant operations."
- **C567** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q213): What is the primary purpose of the Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB)?
  - Answer: Provide the centralized personnel entry and exit point for the major NI facilities.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.6, p. 1.1-20 (PDF page 50)
  - Quote: "The Fuel Auxiliary Building (FAB) is a steel-braced frame structure supported on a concrete grade slab that provides a centralized location for employee and visitor ingress to, and egress from the major NI facilities (RXB, FHB, RAB)."
- **C568** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q214): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island E-Modules?
  - Answer: Contain NI electrical systems and components in prefabricated modules.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.4.8, p. 1.1-21 (PDF page 51)
  - Quote: "Prefabricated E-Modules are located on the NI area to contain electrical systems and components of the electrical systems."
- **C569** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q215): According to the PSAR, which functions does the Reactor Enclosure System (RES) provide during normal and off-normal conditions?
  - Answer: Radionuclide retention, reactivity control, and reactor heat removal.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1, p. 7.1-14 (PDF page 1211)
  - Quote: "The RES provides radionuclide retention, reactivity control, and reactor heat removal functions during normal and off-normal conditions."
- **C570** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q216): Together with the PHT and the RES, the Reactor Air Cooling System (RAC) provides which function?
  - Answer: The long-term emergency core cooling function.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.2.1.1, p. 7.2-1 (PDF page 1280)
  - Quote: "The RAC, in conjunction with the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT) (Section 7.1.3) and the Reactor Enclosure System (RES) (Section 7.1.2), provides the long-term emergency core cooling function."
- **C571** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q218): During a design basis event, how does the Primary Heat Transport System (PHT) support decay heat removal?
  - Answer: It facilitates natural circulation of primary sodium to carry heat to the reactor vessel walls, then to the guard vessel and the RAC.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.4, p. 1.1-4 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "During a design basis event, the PHT safety function is to facilitate natural circulation of the primary sodium to transfer heat from the reactor core to the reactor vessel walls, where the heat is exchanged to the guard vessel and to the RAC."
- **C572** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q219): If pumped flow is lost, how does the Intermediate Heat Transport System (IHT) support decay heat removal?
  - Answer: Natural circulation of intermediate sodium through the IAC sodium-air heat exchangers.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.4.1, p. 7.1-72 (PDF page 1269)
  - Quote: "In the event of a loss of pumped flow, the IHT is designed to provide natural circulation of intermediate coolant for reactor decay heat removal through the IAC Sodium-Air Heat Exchangers (AHXs)."
- **C573** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q220): According to the PSAR, what is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions?
  - Answer: The Intermediate Air Cooling System (IAC).
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.2.2.1, p. 7.2-13 (PDF page 1292)
  - Quote: "The IAC is the primary and preferred means of reactor heat removal during low power and shutdown conditions."
- **C574** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems, from Q221): Which system controls the Control Rod Drive System (CRD) scram function?
  - Answer: The Reactor Protection System (RPS).
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.9, p. 1.1-6 (PDF page 36)
  - Quote: "The scram function is controlled by the RPS."
- **C575** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q222): Why must the Reactor Core System (RCC) maintain its geometry during postulated accidents?
  - Answer: To support the natural circulation flowpath through the core and allow control rod insertion for shutdown.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.1.2, p. 7.1-6 (PDF page 1203)
  - Quote: "the RCC is designed to maintain its geometry to support the natural circulation flowpath of primary coolant through the reactor core during postulated accidents and to allow for control rod insertion for reactor shutdown during postulated accident conditions."
- **C576** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q223): How does the Anticipatory Automatic Seismic Trip System (AST) scram the reactor?
  - Answer: It sends actuation signals to the Reactor Trip Breakers through an interface device provided by the RPS.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.6.8.1, p. 7.6-75 (PDF page 1503)
  - Quote: "automatically generates output actuation signals to the Reactor Trip Breakers (RTBs) through the interface device provided by the Reactor Protection System (RPS) when required by seismic conditions."
- **C577** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q224): Where does the Nuclear Instrumentation System (XIS) send its conditioned neutron flux signals?
  - Answer: To the RPS and the NIC, for protective, control and monitoring functions.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.12, p. 1.1-7 (PDF page 37)
  - Quote: "The XIS amplifies and conditions the instrument signals and provides corresponding input signals to the RPS and the NI Control System (NIC) for use in protective, control, and monitoring functions."
- **C578** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q225): Which leak detection parameters does the Reactor Instrumentation System (RIS) provide to the RPS?
  - Answer: Reactor vessel to guard vessel annulus liquid sodium leak detection.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.14, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "RIS also provides the RV-GV annulus liquid sodium leak detection parameters as an input to RPS."
- **C579** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q226): Which Radiation Monitoring System subsystem gives operators early indication of abnormal radiological conditions in a process, such as failed fuel?
  - Answer: Process radiation monitoring.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The process radiation monitoring subsystem strategy is to give operators early indication of abnormal radiological conditions in a plant process that may be an indication of failures within, or external to, the monitored process (e.g., failed fuel detection)."
- **C580** (PSAR: Integrated Controls Systems, from Q227): What is the primary function of the RMS effluent radiation monitoring subsystem?
  - Answer: Protect public health and safety and assure off-site exposure stays within 10 CFR 20 limits.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.1.13, p. 1.1-8 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "The effluent radiation monitoring subsystem’s primary function is to protect the health and safety of the public and to provide assurance that off-site exposure does not exceed 10 CFR 20 limits."
- **C581** (PSAR: Nuclear Heat Supply Systems, from Q228): Why is the annulus between the reactor vessel and guard vessel inerted with argon?
  - Answer: To minimize the potential for sodium-air reaction.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.1.2.1.3, p. 7.1-17 (PDF page 1214)
  - Quote: "The annular space is inerted with argon gas minimizing the potential for sodium-air reaction."
- **C582** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q229): What does transferring core assemblies in a shielded and inert environment provide in the Ex-Vessel Fuel Handling System?
  - Answer: Radiation shielding, radionuclide retention, and a medium for removal of decay heat.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.2.1, p. 7.3-16 (PDF page 1365)
  - Quote: "Transfer of core assemblies in a shielded and inert environment provides radiation shielding, radionuclide retention, and a medium for removal of decay heat."
- **C583** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems, from Q230): Which functions does the Water Pool Fuel Handling System (FHP) provide for stored fuel?
  - Answer: Core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.3.1.1, p. 7.3-1 (PDF page 1350)
  - Quote: "The FHP provides core assembly cooling, spent fuel reactivity control, fission product containment, and radiation shielding."
- **C584** (PSAR: Radwaste Systems, from Q231): Which fundamental safety function does the Gaseous Radwaste Processing System (RWG) support?
  - Answer: Retaining radionuclides.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.4.1.1, p. 7.4-1 (PDF page 1401)
  - Quote: "The RWG is classified as NSRST because it supports the retain radionuclides fundamental safety function, which protects plant personnel and the environment, supports compliance with 10 CFR Part 20, and minimizes radioactive releases."
- **C585** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q232): How does the Reactor Building substructure support decay heat removal during design basis accidents?
  - Answer: It supports and protects the RES and RAC so the geometry for passive residual heat removal is maintained.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.1.1.2, p. 7.8-3 (PDF page 1521)
  - Quote: "the RXB substructure is designed to structurally support and protect the RES and RAC such that the geometry for passive removal of residual heat from the reactor core is maintained during DBAs."
- **C586** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures, from Q233): What radionuclide retention role does the Reactor Auxiliary Building substructure have?
  - Answer: It provides an enveloping boundary for radionuclide retention in the SPS cells.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.8.3.1.2, p. 7.8-19 (PDF page 1537)
  - Quote: "The RAB substructure provides an enveloping boundary for radionuclide retention in the SPS cells."
- **C587** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems, from Q234): In which building does the Nuclear Island HVAC System (NHV) provide a radionuclide retention function as part of the PRA defense line level four functions?
  - Answer: The Reactor Building (RXB).
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 1, Sec. 1.1.4.3.10, p. 1.1-14 (PDF page 44)
  - Quote: "NHV provides a radionuclide retention function as part of the PRA defense line level four functions in the RXB."
- **C588** (PSAR: Electrical Systems, from Q235): Which CRD function does the NI Uninterruptible AC Power Supply System (NUP) power through the control rod drive motor controllers?
  - Answer: The scram follow motor drive-in function.
  - Source: ML24088A065, Ch. 7, Sec. 7.7.1.1, p. 7.7-1 (PDF page 1509)
  - Quote: "Control rod drive motor controllers (for scram follow motor drive-in function)"

Item reports fill in the item ID, topic, question, and source. The address is set once in feedback.js, and every link stays hidden while it is empty.

## 2026-11-04: PSAR Revision 1 (ML25276A288)

Replaced PSAR Rev 0 (ML24088A065) with Rev 1 at the user's request. The old PDF moved to phone-study-apps-archive/superseded-sources/ outside the project. Details are in PSAR-REV1-REVIEW.md, and the section comparison is in work/psar-revision-changes.md.

Items kept with the same quote: 195. Items with an updated quote: 4. Items removed: 0. New items: 18. Question, option, answer, and explanation text of existing items is unchanged. No PSAR figures are used, so no images changed.

### Updated quotes

- **Q187**: What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Old quote: "The NMV supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
  - New quote: "The NMV receives power from the unit auxiliary transformer or the reserve auxiliary transformer and supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 48)
- **Q188**: What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV) as described in the PSAR?
  - Old quote: "The NLV supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
  - New quote: "The NLV receives power from the NMV and supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 48)
- **C541**: What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Medium Voltage System (NMV)?
  - Old quote: "The NMV supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
  - New quote: "The NMV receives power from the unit auxiliary transformer or the reserve auxiliary transformer and supplies power to the medium voltage loads, 6.9kV-480V transformers, and adjustable speed drives for the PSPs and ISPs."
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 48)
- **C542**: What is the primary purpose of the NI AC Electrical Power Low Voltage System (NLV)?
  - Old quote: "The NLV supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
  - New quote: "The NLV receives power from the NMV and supplies power to the 480V switchgears, 480V Motor Control Center (MCC), and 480V switchboards and panelboards for NI plant auxiliary loads."
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.6, p. 1.1-13 (PDF page 48)

### Flag added

- **Q96** (How is cesium concentration in the primary sodium monitored?): Rev 1 Sec. 1.1.4.1.8 lists oxygen and hydrogen sensors, but Secs. 7.2.4.1 and 7.2.4.3.2 list hydrogen sensors and meters only.

### New items

- **Q478** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Major Maintenance Equipment (NME) as described in the PSAR?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.19, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 53)
  - Quote: "Nuclear Island Major Maintenance Equipment (NME) is used for the installation and removal of the IVTM and FTL to support refueling operations."
- **C589** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components): What is the primary purpose of the Nuclear Island Major Maintenance Equipment (NME)?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.19, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 53)
  - Quote: "Nuclear Island Major Maintenance Equipment (NME) is used for the installation and removal of the IVTM and FTL to support refueling operations."
- **C590** (PSAR: Significant Support Systems and Components): Why does the NME provide an inert environment?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 1.1.4.3.19, p. 1.1-18 (PDF page 53)
  - Quote: "The NME is designed to provide an inert environment to prevent excess air ingress into the primary cover gas space and prevent excess leakage into the Reactor Building during reactor operating mode 4."
- **Q479** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures): What does the Reactor Building (RXB) superstructure structurally support?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.8.1.2, p. 7.8-7 (PDF page 1568)
  - Quote: "The RXB superstructure provides structural support for a single-failure proof overhead bridge crane for movement of equipment and other heavy loads for maintenance within the facility"
- **C591** (PSAR: Buildings and Structures): What is the Reactor Building (RXB) superstructure?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.8.1.2, p. 7.8-7 (PDF page 1568)
  - Quote: "The RXB superstructure is an above-grade steel framed structure supported on concrete foundation independent from the RXB substructure."
- **C592** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): What do guard pipes do in the event of a sodium leak?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.1.3, p. 8.2-2 (PDF page 1615)
  - Quote: "Guard pipes act as a full secondary pressure boundary in the event of a leak and are designed to the same conditions as the protected system pipe."
- **C593** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): What is a sodium catch pan?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.1.6, p. 8.2-2 (PDF page 1615)
  - Quote: "Catch pans are a steel-lined volume designed to retain the design-basis sodium leak volume plus margin."
- **C594** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): What is a clamshell in the sodium leak design?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.5.2.3.4, p. 7.5-15 (PDF page 1466)
  - Quote: "A clamshell is a form of guard enclosure placed specifically where piping inspections are expected to be needed."
- **C595** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): What is a cell in the sodium fire protection design?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.5.2.3.4, p. 7.5-15 (PDF page 1466)
  - Quote: "Cells are rooms with a limited leak rate and known oxygen volume which is either actively inerted or becomes de facto inerted upon consumption of the limited available oxygen after a sodium leak."
- **C596** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): What provides supplemental sodium leak detection in non-inerted fire areas?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.1.8, p. 8.2-3 (PDF page 1616)
  - Quote: "Conventional fire detection installed in non-inerted fire areas provides supplemental sodium leak detection."
- **Q480** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): Besides mitigating sodium-air and sodium-concrete reactions, what do catch pans provide?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.5.2.3.4, p. 7.5-16 (PDF page 1467)
  - Quote: "Catch pans mitigate the effects of sodium-air and sodium-concrete reactions and provide a location where leaked sodium can safely cool."
- **Q481** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): The Natrium sodium fire protection strategy uses which elements?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.2, p. 8.2-3 (PDF page 1616)
  - Quote: "The sodium fire protection strategy is based on a defense-in-depth fire protection design approach and utilizes leak prevention, detection and passive mitigation."
- **Q482** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): Why may sodium-air reactions occur within guard enclosures?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.2.2, p. 8.2-4 (PDF page 1617)
  - Quote: "Sodium-air reactions may occur within guard enclosures as they are not inerted."
- **Q483** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): In a process cell with an inerted environment, what is true of the catch pan?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.2.3, p. 8.2-4 (PDF page 1617)
  - Quote: "For process cells which have an inerted environment, the catch pan does not have a suppression deck."
- **Q484** (PSAR: Ancillary Systems): Why is no suppression deck provided on catch pans for operational leakage?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 8.2.2.1, p. 8.2-4 (PDF page 1617)
  - Quote: "No suppression deck is provided since significant sodium-air reaction is not expected."
- **C597** (PSAR: Reactor Auxiliary Systems): What does the plugging temperature indicator (PTI) provide in the Sodium Processing System?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 7.2.4.3.1, p. 7.2-51 (PDF page 1369)
  - Quote: "The PTI will use this correlation to continuously monitor the plugging temperature of the sodium, providing real-time indication of the overall sodium chemistry."
- **C598** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems): Where are new core assemblies placed after removal from the shipping container?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 3.14.2.5, p. 3.14-6 (PDF page 1078)
  - Quote: "The core assemblies will be removed from the shipping container and placed in the assembly receipt inspection stand (ARIS)."
- **Q485** (PSAR: Fuel Handling Systems): Where is a new core assembly placed after receipt inspection is complete?
  - Source: PSAR Rev 1, ML25276A288, Sec. 3.14.2.5, p. 3.14-6 (PDF page 1078)
  - Quote: "After receipt inspection is complete, each core assembly is removed and placed into the NAPS."

- **C599** (Thermodynamic Units and Properties): What are the three unit conversion steps?
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Unit Conversion, CP-01 p. 16 (PDF page 34)
  - Quote: "Step 1 - Select the equivalent relationship from the conversion table." / "Step 2 - Express the relationship as a conversion factor." / "Step 3 - Multiply the given quantity by the conversion factor."
- **Q486** (Thermodynamic Units and Properties): Which units are the standard units of the MKS form of the SI system?
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Fundamental Dimensions, CP-01 p. 8 (PDF page 26)
  - Quote: "The SI system of measurement consists of the following standard units:" / "MKS" / "Meter" / "Kilogram"

  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Scalar and Vector Quantities, CP-02 p. 1 (PDF page 45)
  - Quote: "Magnitude only" / "Both magnitude and direction"
- **Q487** (Basic Energy Concepts): What is a resultant?
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Vector Terminology, CP-02 p. 15 (PDF page 59)
  - Quote: "A resultant is a single vector that can replace two or more vectors."
- **C601** (Basic Energy Concepts): What is weight?
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Force and Weight, CP-04 p. 4 (PDF page 104)
  - Quote: "Weight is the force exerted on an object due to gravity."
- **Q488** (Basic Energy Concepts): The work done by a force on an object is the product of the force and:
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Energy and Work, CP-05 p. 5 (PDF page 135)
  - Quote: "The work done by a force on an object is the product of the force and the distance the object moves in the direction of the force."
- **Q489** (Basic Energy Concepts): Power is the amount of energy used:
  - Source: DOE-1010 (DOE-HDBK-1010-92), Power, CP-05 p. 11 (PDF page 141)
  - Quote: "Power is the amount of energy used per unit time."

- **C603** (Motors and Generators): How is a capacitor constructed?
  - Source: DOE-1011-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1011/2-92), Capacitance, ES-03 p. 18 (PDF page 38)
  - Quote: "A capacitor is constructed of two conductors (plates) separated by a dielectric."
- **C604** (Motors and Generators): How are capacitors combined in series and in parallel?
  - Source: DOE-1011-V2 (DOE-HDBK-1011/2-92), Capacitance, ES-03 p. 13 (PDF page 33)
  - Quote: "Capacitors in series are combined like resistors in parallel." / "Capacitors in parallel are combined like resistors in series."
- **C605** (Motors and Generators): How do effective (RMS) AC current and voltage relate to their maximum values?
  - Source: DOE-1011-V3 (DOE-HDBK-1011/3-92), Voltage, Current, and Frequency, ES-07 p. 10 (PDF page 30)

- **C606** (Motors and Generators): What is phase angle used for?

  - Source: DOE-1019-V1 (DOE-HDBK-1019/1-93), Nuclear Cross Sections and Neutron Flux, NP-02 p. 17 (PDF page 121)
